title: Advanced Topics in Modeling and Data Analysis: High Dimensional Statistics
weeklyTopics: Linear model with n << p, sparsity, Lasso
l1-regularized logistic regression, GLMs with l1 regularization, l1-SVMs and margins
Matrix completion and trace norm; 1-bit and non-negative matrix completion
Gaussian graphical model selection (l1-regularized log-det, parallel l1-regularized regressions)
Sparse PCA: ScoTLASS, SDP relaxation, generalized power method
High dimensional k-means and sparse subspace clustering
Lasso l2 error bounds, restricted eigenvalue (RE) condition
Sup-norm error bounds and sign consistency of Lasso, mutual incoherence condition
Proximal methods, prox operators, convergence rates
Coordinate descent methods, LARS and the Lasso modification of LARS
Estimation of high-dimensional low-rank matrices, restricted strong convexity (RSC)
Random matrix theory: bounds on maximum singular value, Gordon's theorem, Gaussian concentration for Lipschitz functions
High-dimensional Fisher's LDA, naive Bayes/independence rule, loss-based classification
workloadNotes: Advanced PhD-level course. 4 equally-weighted homeworks mixing theory and programming (60%); final project (40%) is either an individually-written high-quality survey of an actively developing sub-topic, or a research project (teams up to 2) contributing novel theory/methods/algorithms/applications, split into a proposal, presentation, and report. No official programming language required.
